tips.title: Smoke and carbon monoxide alarms
tips.summary: Working alarms are the cheapest lifesaver in your house.
tips: Put a smoke alarm on every level, inside each bedroom, and outside sleeping areas.
Put carbon monoxide alarms on every level and near sleeping areas.
Test alarms monthly. Replace batteries as needed.
Alarms wear out. Check the date on the back and replace the unit when it is 10 years old, or sooner if the maker says so.

tips.title: Plan your escape
tips.summary: A few minutes of planning makes everyone faster when it counts.
tips: Know two ways out of every room.
Pick a meeting spot outside, like the mailbox or a tree.
Practice the plan with everyone in the house, twice a year.
Once you are out, stay out. Call 911 from outside.

tips.title: Wood stoves and chimneys
tips.summary: Before the first fire of the season, check the chimney.
tips: Have chimneys and stovepipes inspected and cleaned before heating season.
Keep anything that burns at least three feet from the stove.
Put ashes in a metal container with a lid, and keep it outside and away from the house.

tips.title: Generators and carbon monoxide
tips.summary: Outages are when generator accidents happen.
tips: Run a generator outdoors only, well away from doors, windows, and vents. Never in a garage, basement, or porch.
Make sure your carbon monoxide alarms work before the storm.
Let the generator cool before refueling.

tips.title: Holiday decorations
tips: Keep a live tree watered and away from heaters and fireplaces.
Check light strings for damage, and do not overload outlets.
Blow out candles when you leave the room.

tips.title: Kitchen fires
tips.summary: Cooking is a leading cause of home fires.
tips: Stay in the kitchen while you are frying, boiling, or broiling.
Keep towels, packaging, and pot holders away from the burners.
If a pan catches fire, slide a lid over it and turn off the heat. Never use water on a grease fire.

tips.title: Lithium-ion batteries
tips.summary: E-bikes, scooters, tools, and phones all run on them.
tips: Use the charger that came with the device, or one approved by its maker.
Do not charge while you sleep or while no one is home. Do not charge on a bed or couch.
Stop using a battery that swells, leaks, smells, or gets very hot.

tips.title: Grilling
tips.summary: Grills belong outside and away from the house.
tips: Use a grill only outdoors, at least ten feet from the house, deck rails, and overhanging branches.
Never leave a lit grill alone.
Keep children and pets well back.

tips.title: Dry-season brush fires
tips.summary: Dry grass and leaves burn fast.
tips: Never burn without a permit. Burn permits come from the Town Fire Marshal, not from us.
Do not throw cigarettes out a car window or leave them in mulch or planters.
If a brush fire gets away from you, call 911 right away.

basics.title: 911 or non-emergency?
basics.text: If someone is in danger or there is a fire, call 911. For non-emergency questions, call (203) 393-2799 or use the contact page.

basics.title: Make your house number easy to see
basics.text: Large, reflective numbers visible from the road help us find you quickly, day or night.

basics.title: Storm and outage prep
basics.text: Charge phones, keep flashlights handy, and know where your generator will run before the storm, not during it.
